He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton Bluejays]]. Following his college career, Alexander signed with the [[Phoenix Suns]] in November 2020 after going undrafted in the [[2020 NBA draft]]. During his rookie season with the Suns, he reached the [[NBA Finals]]. Since leaving the Suns, he has split his career between playing the NBA G League and with various teams in Europe. In 2021 he won the [[Italian Basketball Supercup|Italian Supercup]] with [[Virtus Bologna]] and in 2023 he won the [[List of NBA G League champions|NBA G League championship with]] the [[Delaware Blue Coats]]. Alexander was a member of the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]] that finished third at the [[Basketball at the 2019 Pan American Games – Men's tournament|2019 Pan American Games in Lima]]. ==High school career== Alexander attended [[Concord High School (North Carolina)|Concord High School]] his freshman year and was named to the All-South Piedmont 3A Conference team and earned honorable mention on MaxPreps.com's Freshman All-American Team. He transferred to [[Northside Christian Academy]] in [[Charlotte, North Carolina]] as a sophomore. As a junior, he moved on to [[Oak Hill Academy (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]].{{cite news |last1=Nyatawa |first1=Jon |title=Alexander succeeding at Creighton but wants to be better |url=https://www.independenttribune.com/ty-shon-alexander-story-page-b/article_f7e5e301-6a28-5718-b51e-771d4b32bd40.html |access-date=January 26, 2020 |work=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |publisher=Independent Tribune}} Alexander scored 50 points in a game as a senior. He averaged 14.1 points per game as a senior, shooting 46.3 percent from behind the arc.{{cite news |last1=Nyatawa |first1=Jon |title=Want to watch Creighton basketball recruits Ty-Shon Alexander and Jacob Epperson? Turn on the Dick's Nationals prep tournament |url=https://www.omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/want-to-watch-creighton-basketball-recruits-ty-shon-alexander-and/article_8ec52f1e-5cdc-5074-9e84-d358fdf0251f.html |access-date=January 26, 2020 |work=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |date=March 29, 2017}} He was considered a four-star recruit and was ranked No. 85 in his class by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]]. Alexander committed to [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]] on October 31, 2015, turning down offers from [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball|Clemson]], [[Charlotte 49ers men's basketball|Charlotte]] and [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]].{{cite magazine |title=Report: Four-star guard Ty-Shon Alexander commits to Creighton |url=https://www.si.com/college/2015/10/31/tyshon-alexander-creighton-recruiting |access-date=January 26, 2020 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=October 31, 2015}} ==College career== On November 20, 2017, Alexander was named [[Big East Conference|Big East]] freshman of the week after registering 14 points, three rebounds and two assists in a 92–88 victory over [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.bigeast.com/news/2017/11/20/mens-basketball-xaviers-bluiett-creightons-alexander-take-mbb-weekly-honors.aspx?path=mbball |title=Xavier's Bluiett, Creighton's Alexander Take MBB Weekly Honors |website=[[Big East Conference]] |date=November 20, 2017 |access-date=January 26, 2020}} He posted 5.5 points, 2.1 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game as a freshman playing backup to [[Marcus Foster (basketball)|Marcus Foster]].{{cite news |last1=Nyatawa |first1=Jon |title=25 Days of Jays: No. 25 Ty-Shon Alexander |url=https://www.omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/days-of-jays-no-ty-shon-alexander/article_4bed164e-639f-5a5f-b572-2e511633f9e9.html |access-date=January 26, 2020 |work=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |date=July 26, 2018}} In the offseason after his freshman year, Alexander made a point to take 100 shots before bed and work on his shooting technique in order to become Creighton's next great scorer.{{cite news |last1=Nyatawa |first1=Jon |title=Ty-Shon Alexander made a point this offseason to become Creighton's next great scorer |url=https://www.omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/ty-shon-alexander-made-a-point-this-offseason-to-become/article_ef200e73-26f0-5afc-aa27-f9ea43f34c4b.html |access-date=January 26, 2020 |work=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |date=September 24, 2018}} Alexander scored a career-high 36 points on November 22, 2018, in a 87–82 win against [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball|Clemson]].{{cite news |title=Ty-Shon Alexander scores career-high 36 points to help Creighton upset No. 16 Clemson |url=https://www.omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/ty-shon-alexander-scores-career-high-points-to-help-creighton/article_281176d8-83e0-5c70-95cd-21cd360ab308.html |access-date=January 26, 2020 |work=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |date=November 22, 2018}} He was named Big East player of the week on January 28, 2019, after contributing 26 points, seven rebounds, and four assists in a 91–87 win against [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.bigeast.com/news/2019/1/28/mens-basketball-creightons-alexander-marquettes-hauser-earn-bigeastmbb-weekly-honors.aspx |title=Creighton's Alexander, Marquette's Hauser Earn #BIGEASTmbb Weekly Honors |website=[[Big East Conference]] |date=January 28, 2019 |access-date=January 26, 2020}} As a sophomore, Alexander averaged 15.7 points, 4.0 rebounds and 2.7 assists per game. Alexander was an All-Big East Honorable Mention selection alongside teammate [[Martin Krampelj]].{{cite news |last1=Nyatawa |first1=Jon |title=Two Bluejays earn All-Big East honorable mention status; Zegarowski named to all-freshman team |url=https://www.omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/two-bluejays-earn-all-big-east-honorable-mention-status-zegarowski/article_cec72f7c-eedb-549f-bf66-c678a43c8426.html |access-date=January 26, 2020 |work=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |date=March 10, 2019}} Alexander surpassed the 1,000 point mark in a loss to Georgetown on January 16, 2020, finishing with 14 points.{{cite news |last1=Tjaden |first1=Joe |title=25th ranked Creighton men's basketball drops road game at Georgetown |url=https://norfolkdailynews.com/wjag/sports/th-ranked-creighton-men-s-basketball-drops-road-game-at/article_352ae50c-3862-11ea-8eb3-5ffae9a6c825.html |access-date=January 26, 2020 |work=[[Norfolk Daily News]] |date=January 16, 2020}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Alexander was named to the First Team All-Big East.{{cite news |last1=Smith |first1=Rex |title=Alexander, Zegarowski named to All-BIG EAST teams |url=https://www.wowt.com/content/news/Alexander-Zegarowski-named-to-All-BIG-EAST-teams-568609421.html |access-date=March 8, 2020 |work=WOWT |date=March 8, 2020}} As a junior, Alexander averaged 16.9 points, 5.0 rebounds, 2.3 assists, and 1.3 steals per game, finishing second in the Big East in free throw percentage at 86 percent and sixth in the conference at three-point shooting at 39.9 percent.{{cite web |title=NABC Honors Alexander, Zegarowski and McDermott |url=https://gocreighton.com/news/2020/3/23/mens-basketball-nabc-honors-alexander-zegarowski-and-mcdermott.aspx |website=[[Creighton Bluejays]] |access-date=March 24, 2020 |date=March 23, 2020}} Following the season, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last1=Dauster |first1=Rob |title=Creighton's Ty-Shon Alexander declares for NBA draft |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2020/04/10/creightons-ty-shon-alexander-declares-for-nba-draft/ |access-date=April 11, 2020 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=April 10, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Phoenix Suns (2020–2021)=== After going undrafted in the [[2020 NBA draft]], Alexander signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite news |last1=Boan |first1=Christopher |title=Suns signing undrafted guard Ty-Shon Alexander to 2-way contract |url=https://arizonasports.com/story/2454918/suns-signing-undrafted-guard-ty-shon-alexander-to-2-way-contract/ |access-date=November 19, 2020 |work=Arizona Sports |date=November 19, 2020}} Alexander made his NBA debut on December 27, 2020, in a 116–100 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]]. He got a rebound and an assist two days later in a blowout 111–86 win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]. Since the Phoenix Suns did not assign their [[Northern Arizona Suns]] franchise to the 2021 [[NBA G League]] Bubble at the [[ESPN Wide World of Sports Complex]] in [[Orlando, Florida|Orlando]], his G League rights were transferred to the [[Canton Charge]] for his rookie season.[https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/nba/canton-charge-add-four-players-as-nba-g-league-training-camp-approaches/ar-BB1ddInA Canton Charge add four players as NBA G League training camp approaches] Alexander made it to the [[2021 NBA Finals]], but the Suns lost in 6 games to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. On August 26, 2021, he was waived by the Suns.{{cite news |last1=Scott |first1=Dana |title=Suns waive guard Ty-Shon Alexander |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2021/08/26/suns-waive-second-year-guard-ty-shon-alexander/5610698001/ |access-date=August 28, 2021 |work=AZCentral |date=August 26, 2021}} ===Virtus Bologna (2021–2022)=== In September 2021, Alexander signed a two-year deal with [[Virtus Bologna]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA).[https://www.virtus.it/news/ty-shon-leron-alexander-e-un-nuovo-giocatore-di-virtus-segafredo-bologna/ Ty-Shon Alexander è un nuovo giocatore di Virtus Segafredo Bologna], ''Virtus Segafredo Bologna'' On 21 September, the team won its second [[2021 Italian Basketball Supercup|Supercup]], defeating [[Olimpia Milano]] 90–84.[https://www.repubblica.it/sport/basket/2021/09/21/news/basket_supercoppa_alla_virtus_bologna_il_primo_trofeo_stagionale_milano_ancora_ko-318837432/ Basket, la Virtus Bologna vince la Supercoppa: Milano ancora ko], ''la Repubblica'' However, on 15 February 2022, Alexander and the club agreed on ending the contract.{{cite web |title=Ty-Shon Alexander, risoluzione consensuale |url=https://www.virtus.it/news/ty-shon-alexander-risoluzione-consensuale/ |website=virtus.it |date=15 February 2022}} ===Pallacanestro Trieste (2022)=== On 15 February 2022, Alexander was signed by [[Pallacanestro Trieste]], another team of LBA.[https://www.pallacanestrotrieste.it/news/513363316230/ty-shon-alexander-egrave-biancorosso TY-SHON ALEXANDER È BIANCOROSSO!], ''Pallacanestro Trieste'' ===Greensboro Swarm (2022–2023)=== Alexander joined the [[Charlotte Hornets]] for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite web |title=Charlotte Hornets 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612766/hornets |access-date=July 5, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} He later joined the [[Greensboro Swarm]] training camp roster. On November 4, 2022, he was named to the opening night roster.{{cite web |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/greensboro-swarm-announce-2022-23-opening-night-roster/n-5895692 |title=Greensboro Swarm Announce 2022-23 Opening Night Roster |website=oursportscentral.com |date=November 4, 2022 |access-date=November 4, 2022}} ===Delaware Blue Coats (2023)=== On February 24, 2023, Alexander was traded to the [[Delaware Blue Coats]],{{cite web |url=https://gleague.nba.com/22-23-nba-g-league-transactions |website=gleague.nba.com |title=2022-23 NBA G League Transactions |date=February 24, 2023 |access-date=February 24, 2023}} and eventually helped the team win the [[NBA G League]] title.{{cite web |first=Noah |last=Levick |title=Delaware Blue Coats win G League championship; Jaden Springer named Finals MVP |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/sixers/delaware-blue-coats-nba-g-league-championship-2023-jaden-springer-mac-mcclung |website=NBCSports.com |date=April 7, 2023 |access-date=April 7, 2023}} ===Koroivos (2023–2024)=== On November 22, 2023, he joined [[Koroivos B.C.|Koroivos]] of the [[Greek A2 Basket League|Greek A2 Elite League]]. He went on to average 17.5 points per game, being one of the best players in the league. ===Panionios (2024)=== On June 26, 2024, he joined [[Panionios B.C.|Panionios]] of the [[Greek Basket League]]. He left the team without appearing in a single game for them. ===Keflavík (2024–2025)=== On November 13, 2024, Alexander signed with [[Keflavík men's basketball|Keflavík]] of the Icelandic [[Úrvalsdeild karla (basketball)|Úrvalsdeild karla]].{{cite news |author1=Stefán Árni Pálsson |title=Keflavík semur við leikmann sem hefur skorað tvö stig í úrslitaeinvígi NBA |url=https://www.visir.is/g/20242649089d/keflavik-semur-vid-leikmann-sem-hefur-skorad-tvo-stig-i-urslitaeinvigi-nba |access-date=13 November 2024 |work=[[Vísir.is]] |date=13 November 2024 |language=Icelandic}} During the regular season, he averaged 20.5 points, 4.9 rebounds and 4.5 assists. On 27 March 2025, he scored a season high 38 points in Keflavík's 119–114 win against [[Þór Þorlákshöfn (basketball)|Þór Þorlákshöfn]] in the last game of the regular season, securing the final berth in the playoffs.{{cite news |author1=Hjörvar Ólafsson |title=Uppgjörið: Þór - Keflavík 114-119 - Keflvíkingar tryggðu sér sæti í úrslitakeppninni |url=https://www.visir.is/g/20252706839d/i-beinni-thor-kefla-vik-ogur-stund-i-thor-laks-hofn |access-date=21 April 2025 |work=[[Vísir.is]] |date=27 March 2025 |language=Icelandic}} In the playoffs, he averaged 18.3 points, 3.7 rebounds and 7.0 assists in Keflavík's 0–3 first round loss against [[Tindastóll men's basketball|Tindastóll]]. ==National team career== In the summer of 2019, Alexander was a part of the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States National team]] who competed at the [[Basketball at the 2019 Pan American Games – Men's tournament|Pan American Games]] in Peru.{{cite news |last1=Nyatawa |first1=Jon |title=Current Bluejay Ty-Shon Alexander and former CU center Geoffery Groselle selected for Pan-Am games |url=https://www.omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/current-bluejay-ty-shon-alexander-and-former-cu-center-geoffery/article_05f0c59c-91c1-54b0-a7c9-42662b32b4a8.html |access-date=January 26, 2020 |work=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |date=June 19, 2019}} The team won bronze.{{cite news |url=https://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2019/08/mpag-game-5.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190806170036/https://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2019/08/mpag-game-5.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 6, 2019 |title=U.S. Men Rally To Win Bronze Medal at Pan American Games |publisher=[[USA Basketball]] |date=August 4, 2019 |access-date=November 10, 2019}} ==Personal life== Alexander is the son of Eric and Tina Alexander. He has one brother, Rodjrick.{{cite web |title=Ty-Shon Alexander - 2019-20 - Men's Basketball |url=https://gocreighton.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/ty-shon-alexander/6372 |website=Creighton
